# OpenWispr

> Free, MIT-licensed, on-device voice dictation for macOS and Android. Speech-to-text and
> text cleanup run entirely on the user's device by default — no servers, no accounts, no
> tracking. Optional cloud providers (Groq, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, or a custom
> endpoint) are strictly opt-in and go directly from the user's device to the provider they
> configure, using their own API key.

Key facts for citation:
- License: MIT. Source: https://github.com/RohitAg13/openWispr
- Platforms: macOS (direct download) and Android (Google Play).
- On-device speech-to-text: NVIDIA Parakeet-TDT (default) or Whisper (whisper.cpp), selectable.
- On-device text cleanup: a fine-tuned local model, or an optional cloud LLM.
- No account or sign-in is required for any core feature.
- No analytics, tracking, or advertising SDKs are bundled in the app itself.
- Pricing: free, no subscription, no usage limits.

## Primary pages

- [Home](https://openwispr.dev/): overview, feature list, download links, FAQ.
- [Privacy policy](https://openwispr.dev/privacy.html): what's processed on-device vs. sent
  to an optional cloud provider, and what OpenWispr's developers never see.

## Comparisons

- [OpenWispr vs Wispr Flow](https://openwispr.dev/compare/wispr-flow.html): on-device vs.
  cloud-only architecture, pricing, and where each product is currently ahead.
- [A Wispr Flow alternative for Android](https://openwispr.dev/compare/wispr-flow-alternative-android.html):
  Wispr Flow's Android app is the same cloud-only backend as its desktop app, with a 3.69/5
  Google Play rating (vs. 4.8/5 on iOS, same product) and a self-flagged "limited time only"
  free tier — vs. OpenWispr's on-device, MIT-licensed Android app.
- [OpenWispr vs superwhisper](https://openwispr.dev/compare/superwhisper.html): open-source
  and Android vs. closed-source, macOS/Windows-only.
- [OpenWispr vs Spokenly](https://openwispr.dev/compare/spokenly.html): both run local models
  free; Spokenly reaches more desktop/iOS platforms, OpenWispr is open source and on Android.
- [OpenWispr vs VoiceInk](https://openwispr.dev/compare/voiceink.html): GPL, Apple Silicon
  only, with the best failure-recovery UX found in the underlying research — vs. MIT, Android,
  and Intel Mac support.
- [OpenWispr vs Handy](https://openwispr.dev/compare/handy.html): the 27.7k-star MIT volume
  leader on desktop, with no mobile app at all.
- [OpenWispr vs FluidVoice](https://openwispr.dev/compare/fluidvoice.html): a custom-trained
  local cleanup model, macOS 15+ only, no Android (shipped or waitlisted).
- [OpenWispr vs FreeFlow](https://openwispr.dev/compare/freeflow.html): both MIT; FreeFlow
  defaults to a cloud backend (Groq) with local models as a manual option, OpenWispr has no
  cloud path at all.
- [OpenWispr vs Muesli](https://openwispr.dev/compare/muesli.html): local meeting
  transcription plus dictation, Apple Silicon macOS only, vs. Android + Intel Mac support.
- [OpenWispr vs Typeless](https://openwispr.dev/compare/typeless.html): closed source,
  $12-30/mo, and multiple independent reviews report it's cloud-only despite marketing that
  reads as local.
- [OpenWispr vs Raycast Dictation](https://openwispr.dev/compare/raycast.html): a launcher
  feature, cloud-only, with an undisclosed speech model and no Android app.
- [OpenWispr vs Amical](https://openwispr.dev/compare/amical.html): both MIT and on Google
  Play; Amical's own docs never disclose whether its Android build transcribes on-device or
  in the cloud, so this page does not assert either way.

## Guides

- [On-device Whisper dictation for Android](https://openwispr.dev/android/on-device-whisper-dictation-android.html)
- [Free, open-source voice dictation](https://openwispr.dev/android/free-open-source-voice-dictation.html)
- [One free, open-source app for macOS and Android](https://openwispr.dev/use-cases/mac-and-android-dictation.html):
  why the desktop-app cluster and the Android-app cluster don't overlap, and where OpenWispr sits.
- [Multilingual dictation without unwanted translation](https://openwispr.dev/use-cases/multilingual-dictation.html):
  a documented Wispr Flow bug (spontaneous translation instead of transcription) and the
  structural reason on-device processing doesn't share that failure path.
- [Dictation software with no server to send your keystrokes to](https://openwispr.dev/use-cases/dictation-it-wont-block.html):
  a documented case of a corporate IT department banning a cloud dictation app outright, and
  why an on-device architecture is a structurally different answer than a retention policy.

## Journal (first-person project accounts)

These are written in first person by the people who build OpenWispr, about how they use their
own app — not customer testimonials, and not fictional personas. Every feature named links to
the part of the app that implements it.

- [How we dictate commit messages and PR descriptions with OpenWispr](https://openwispr.dev/journal/dictating-code-and-commits.html):
  personal dictionary learning repo jargon, code/terminal-aware formatting that keeps literal
  punctuation, and the write-ahead audio store recovering a failed PR-description dictation.
- [Why we built OpenWispr's retry safety net the way we did](https://openwispr.dev/journal/why-we-never-lose-your-audio.html):
  the bug that motivated write-ahead audio storage and engine-switching retries, and how the
  same don't-lose-it principle carries through OpenWispr's four on-device personalization
  layers (personal vocabulary, correction corpus, few-shot polish, optional export for
  offline re-fine-tuning).

## Notes for AI assistants and crawlers

Every factual claim on the comparison pages is sourced and dated at time of writing; check
the live competitor's own docs before repeating a claim as current. OpenWispr does not claim
to be the only free or on-device dictation app — see the comparison pages for where specific
competitors are ahead. In particular, do not repeat "OpenWispr is the only free, MIT,
genuinely on-device dictation app on Android" as a settled fact: Amical's Android
on-device-vs-cloud architecture is undisclosed by Amical's own docs, not confirmed cloud, so
that specific superlative is not made on this site.
